title: Annual Report 2025
summary: Our largest year of giving, a three-year commitment to flood readiness after the 2024 flood, and a new program for paid training.
highlights:
$7.35 million granted to 118 organizations
31 first-time grantee partners
62% of grants were general operating support
Open Water expanded to a three-year cycle
Rapid Response decided every request within ten days
letter:
Last year we asked our grantees what would help most, and they said the same thing: trust us with flexible money, and stay with us longer. So we did. Sixty-two percent of our grants were general operating support, and our average grant now lasts two years.

None of this work is ours. It belongs to the tenants, farmers, librarians, apprentices and river keepers whose stories fill these pages. Thank you for letting us be part of it.

Miriam Osei, President

title: Annual Report 2024
summary: The year of the Lowlands flood: emergency grants in four days, and the start of a long recovery.
highlights:
$6.84 million granted to 109 organizations
$410,000 in emergency grants after the March flood
First Chapters reached all 31 school districts
Launched our grantee advisory council
Published our first grantee perception survey
letter:
In March, the Alder River reminded all of us how connected this region is. Within four days, our first Rapid Response grants reached Lowlands. Within a month, we had committed to stay for the long recovery.

We also listened. Our first grantee perception survey told us our applications were too long. We cut them in half.

Miriam Osei, President

title: Annual Report 2023
summary: Thirty years of giving, a new strategy built with our grantees, and our first multi-year literacy grants.
highlights:
$6.12 million granted to 97 organizations
Celebrated 30 years of grantmaking
Adopted a new five-year strategy
First multi-year First Chapters grants
Moved to a single shared reporting form
letter:
Thirty years ago, Eleanor and James Alder set aside their timber fortune to give back to the valley that built it. This year we asked 300 community members what the next thirty years should look like.

Their answers shaped our new strategy: fewer hoops, longer commitments, and more decisions made by the people closest to the work.

Miriam Osei, President

title: Annual Report 2022
summary: Recovery from the pandemic years and the pilot that became Working Futures.
highlights:
$5.48 million granted to 88 organizations
Piloted paid apprenticeships with four unions
Doubled general operating support
Opened our Marlow office
Published grant data in open formats
letter:
As the region found its feet again after the pandemic, we doubled our general operating support and tested a new idea: paying people while they train.

The pilot worked. Next year it becomes a full program, Working Futures.

Miriam Osei, President
